newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CBA says prefers high div to special.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CBA says prefers high div to special.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia chairman Tim Besley said on Wednesday that the bank preferred to continue with its current high dividend payout ratio instead of paying a special dividend.

"It's better to continue with a high level of payout," Besley told a news briefing when asked if the bank was considering a special dividend as had been speculated in the market. "We expect to retain the level of payout," he said.
The bank set a 45 cent dividend for the first half of 1996/97 to December 31, up from 38 cents a year earlier.
This represented a payout ratio of 68.2 percent, up from 67.1 percent a year earlier.
Talk of a special dividend helped push the bank's shares to record highs in recent trading.
The bank earlier reported an 11 percent rise in net profit to A$602 million for the half year.
CBA shares were up 29 cents at A$13.70 at 0020 GMT (11.20 a.m.). The stock hit a record A$13.79 after release of the results.
